content: 1. Ciclodan® Cream is strictly not intended for ophthalmic use. It should be kept out of the reach of children to prevent accidental exposure. 2. If any signs of sensitivity or chemical irritation occur during the use of Ciclodan® Cream, such as redness, itching, burning, blistering, swelling, or oozing, the treatment should be discontinued immediately. Appropriate alternative therapy should be initiated as necessary. 3. Patients are advised to complete the full course of treatment with Ciclodan® Cream, even if symptoms improve before the treatment period ends. If there is no improvement after four weeks of use, the prescribing physician should be notified. 4. Patients should inform their physician if the application site shows increased irritation, such as redness, itching, burning, blistering, swelling, or oozing, as these may indicate possible sensitization. 5. The use of occlusive wrappings or dressings over the treated area should be avoided. 6. A carcinogenicity study conducted in female mice, where Ciclopirox was applied cutaneously twice per week for 50 weeks followed by a 6-month drug-free observation period, showed no evidence of tumor formation at the application site. 7. Genotoxicity tests conducted with Ciclopirox olamine, including the Ames Salmonella/Mammalian Microsome Assay, Yeast Saccharomyces Cerevisiae Assay, Mouse Dominant Lethal Assay, Mouse Micronucleus Assay at 500 mg/kg, and Unscheduled DNA Synthesis Assay in A549 human cells, all yielded negative results, indicating no genotoxic potential. 8. An in vitro Cell Transformation Assay in BALB/C 3T3 cells also showed no evidence of cell transformation. Similarly, an in vivo Chinese Hamster Bone Marrow Cytogenetic Assay demonstrated no chromosomal aberrations at a dose of 5,000 mg/kg. 9. Reproductive studies in mice, rats, rabbits, and monkeys, using doses 10 times or more than the topical human dose, revealed no significant evidence of impaired fertility or harm to the fetus due to Ciclopirox. However, there are no adequate or well-controlled studies in pregnant women. As animal studies are not always predictive of human response, Ciclopirox should only be used during pregnancy if clearly necessary. 10. It is unknown whether Ciclopirox is excreted in human breast milk. Since many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised when Ciclodan® Cream is administered to nursing mothers. 11. The safety and effectiveness of Ciclodan® Cream in pediatric patients under the age of 10 years have not been established.
